title: On 5 July 2026, the OSINT Analyst M0nstas Published an Overlay Comparison of the Maps Published in High-Resolution on the Kremlin Website — Taken from Putin's 3 July Meeting with Gerasimov and Senior Commanders at the Auxiliary Command Post of the Joint Group of Forces — Against the Ukrainian DeepState Project's Territorial-Control Layer, Exposing a 1,900-Square-Kilometer Discrepancy. Putin's On-Record Figure Since 1 January, 'More Than 3,000 Square Kilometers,' Is Contradicted by DeepState's 770 — and by the ISW Assessment Published 5 July That Quantifies Russian Seizures or Infiltrations Since 1 January 2026 at 621.7 Square Kilometers, Roughly One-Fifth of Putin's Claim.
beat: Putin 3,000 sq km vs DeepState 770 — M0nstas 1,900-sq-km overlay + ISW 621.7 YTD quantification vs Kremlin command-post map — July 3-5 2026
narrative: On 5 July 2026, the OSINT analyst M0nstas compared the maps published in high-resolution on the Kremlin website (taken from Putin's 3 July meeting with Gerasimov and senior commanders at the auxiliary command post of the Joint Group of Forces) against the Ukrainian DeepState project's territorial-control layer. The discrepancy between the Russian MoD maps and DeepState is 1,900 square kilometers. On one map, the difference is highlighted in yellow; on the other two, in pink. DeepState's data on Russian-controlled territory is shown in red. The discrepancy in Russian territorial gains between the Ministry of Defense's maps and DeepState 'can be described as an exaggeration,' military analyst Kirill Mikhailov told 'Agency' (cited by Charter'97). The ISW assessment published 5 July corroborates: Russian forces have captured or entered 64 settlements and seized or infiltrated about 621.7 square kilometers (240 square miles) across the theater since the beginning of 2026 — and in June alone, only ~30.42 square kilometers (11.7 square miles). Putin told his commanders the figure since 1 January is 'more than 3,000 square kilometers.' DeepState puts it at 770 square kilometers. The ISW assessment explicitly states the figures do not support the picture presented by Putin. The 5 July statement frames the exaggerated claims as part of Russia's information warfare campaign aimed at 'creating the impression that a Russian victory in Ukraine is inevitable and that Ukraine's front line is on the verge of collapse.' The three independent quantification layers converge on the same under-3,000 km² ceiling: Putin's 'more than 3,000' claim (3 July command-post meeting, on-record), Russian MoD's territorial-control map (3 July, Kremlin website, hi-res post-event), ISW's verified-by-geolocated-imagery 621.7 km² figure since 1 January (5 July assessment). The 3,000-vs-622 gap is roughly 4.8×. The DeepState-vs-MoD map gap is 1,900 km². The 3 July maps were 'blurred' in the livestream of the meeting itself — and only published in hi-res afterwards on the Kremlin website, a sequencing detail that is itself the asymmetry. The reciprocal-numerator-asymmetry pattern (Russia claims 500 intercepted drones overnight; Zelensky claims Kronstadt hit; the documents are not released by either side) is the second-order pattern that makes the 1,900 km² overlay credible.
analysis:
1. The M0nstas 1,900-square-kilometer overlay is the load-bearing public artifact. M0nstas published the comparison on 5 July: the Russian MoD hi-res map overlaid against the DeepState red-layer polygon, with the 1,900 km² delta highlighted in yellow on one map and pink on the other two. The methodology is reproducible — any third-party analyst with access to both data sources can replicate the measurement. The 1,900 km² figure is the measured area of the polygon difference, not an estimate. M0nstas is publicly credited by the Charter'97-cited 'Agency' investigative team. The overlay is the OSINT-artifact anchor; DeepState is the territorial-control-layer anchor; ISW is the named-third-party anchor. Three sources, one conclusion, one quantified discrepancy.

2. The ISW 5 July assessment is the load-bearing named-third-party corroboration. ISW: Russian forces have 'captured or entered 64 settlements and seized or infiltrated about 621.7 square kilometers (240 square miles) across the theater since the beginning of 2026.' June alone: ~30.42 square kilometers (11.7 square miles). ISW explicitly states the figures 'include settlements where Russian forces have only partially infiltrated, but even with that included, they do not support the picture presented by Putin.' The ISW 621.7 km² YTD figure is roughly one-fifth of Putin's 3,000 km² claim. ISW's framing of the exaggeration as part of Russia's information warfare campaign — 'creating the impression that a Russian victory in Ukraine is inevitable and that Ukraine's front line is on the verge of collapse' — is the named information-warfare framing layer.

3. The 3 July command-post meeting sequencing is the asymmetric-transparency anchor. Putin in military uniform, Gerasimov reading success reports against a backdrop of (deliberately) blurry maps, followed by Kremlin website publishing the maps in hi-res hours later. The asymmetry between what the Russian public saw live and what analysts worldwide could measure the next day is itself the structural finding. Prior meetings (27 December, 30 November) followed the same pattern — 27 December was also blurred; 30 November had no maps on the walls. The sequencing detail is itself the asymmetric-transparency mechanism: the live broadcast shows the political event, the post-event hi-res publication shows the documentary footprint that the OSINT layer can measure.

4. Kirill Mikhailov's 'exaggeration' quote is the named Russian-military-analyst anchor. Mikhailov, cited by 'Agency' (the Russian investigative outlet, accessed via Charter'97): the discrepancy in Russian territorial gains between the Ministry of Defense's maps and DeepState 'can be described as an exaggeration.' Mikhailov's statement is on-record, public, and from within the Russian information space — a Russian analyst confirming the OSINT measurement. The 'Agency' investigative team is publicly credited for the M0nstas attribution. The Mikhailov quote is the third-party validation that the 1,900 km² overlay is not a Ukrainian or Western framing artifact but a measurable gap visible to a Russian analyst.

5. The reciprocal-numerator-asymmetry parallel (Ukraine General Staff 4 July disclosure) is the corroboration layer. On 4 July, Russia reported 389-500 intercepted drones overnight across the country; Sobyanin said 62 shot down headed for Moscow; Beglov said 72 over Leningrad; Drozdenko said 72 over Leningrad. Ukraine's General Staff reported that as of early July, 42.74% of Russia's oil refining capacity is disabled (8 refineries hit, 60+ storage tanks destroyed/damaged in the past month). The reciprocal-numerator-asymmetry pattern: Russia claims 500 intercepted, Zelensky claims Kronstadt hit; the documents are not released by either side. The reciprocal pattern (claim a large denial count, claim a large offensive count, release neither document) is the second-order structural fingerprint that makes the 1,900 km² overlay credible as a pattern rather than an isolated discrepancy.

6. The 'flood the information space' ISW framing is the named information-warfare formulation. ISW's 5 July assessment frames the exaggerated territorial-gain claims alongside 64 separate settlement claims, Kostiantynivka 'fully captured' coverage (contradicted by Zelensky + DELTA/Dzvin), Luhansk 'liberation' claims, and the fortress-belt 'breakthrough' framing. The cumulative count of unverified territorial and settlement claims is the named information-warfare pattern, and the 1,900 km² overlay is the load-bearing quantified artifact that converts the pattern from a narrative framing into a measurable discrepancy.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: On 5 July 2026, the OSINT analyst M0nstas published an overlay comparison of the maps published in high-resolution on the Kremlin website — taken from Putin's 3 July meeting with Gerasimov and senior commanders at the auxiliary command post of the Joint Group of Forces — against the Ukrainian DeepState project's territorial-control layer, exposing a 1,900-square-kilometer discrepancy. Putin's on-record figure since 1 January, 'more than 3,000 square kilometers,' is contradicted by DeepState's 770 and by the ISW assessment published 5 July that quantifies Russian seizures or infiltrations since 1 January 2026 at 621.7 square kilometers — roughly one-fifth of Putin's claim. The 3,000-vs-622 gap is approximately 4.8×. The 3 July maps were blurred in the livestream of the meeting itself and only published in hi-res afterwards on the Kremlin website, an asymmetric-transparency sequencing detail. Military analyst Kirill Mikhailov, cited by 'Agency' via Charter'97, confirmed the discrepancy 'can be described as an exaggeration.' ISW frames the cumulative 64-settlement + 621.7 km² YTD + ~30.42 km² June figures as not supporting the picture presented by Putin and as part of Russia's information warfare campaign to 'create the impression that a Russian victory in Ukraine is inevitable.' The empirical floor: M0nstas 1,900 km² overlay (yellow/pink delta on Russian MoD hi-res map vs DeepState red layer) + ISW 621.7 km² YTD + ISW ~30.42 km² June + DeepState 770 + Putin's 3,000 + Mikhailov 'exaggeration' quote + 3 July command-post blurred-vs-hi-res sequencing + ISW 'flood the information space' framing + Ukraine General Staff 4 July reciprocal-numerator-asymmetry disclosure. The load-bearing finding: the quantified discrepancy is measurable from primary-source documents (Russian MoD hi-res map + DeepState red layer), reproducible by any third-party analyst, corroborated by ISW's independent 621.7 km² YTD figure, and validated by a Russian military analyst's 'exaggeration' quote. The structural inversion: the live broadcast showed the political event (Putin + Gerasimov at the command post); the post-event hi-res Kremlin website publication showed the documentary footprint that the OSINT layer can measure against an independent territorial-control source. The 1,900 km² overlay is not a Ukrainian or Western framing artifact — it is a measurable polygon difference between two named territorial-control sources that a Russian analyst publicly confirms. The prior Kostiantynivka 'fully captured' coverage (4 July) sits on a different evidence layer (city-control frame) — this article covers the theater-level quantified exaggeration layer, primary-source-anchored to M0nstas and ISW.
